author: Day Tripping Quiz

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Standing on legs in the Cathedral's shadow
stops.Hint_1: I was built to celebrate a King restored.
stops.Hint_2: Look for an open-air building resting on stone pillars in the main square.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Find the stone structure in Cathedral Square with the date 1671. This is the Guildhall. It was built in 1671 by the city to commemorate the restoration of King Charles II to the throne. It originally housed a butter market beneath it.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Three massive arches reach for the sky
stops.Hint_1: guarding the grave of a tragic Queen.
stops.Hint_2: Walk towards the largest building in the city.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Stand before the three massive gothic arches of the Cathedral. This is the spectacular West Front of Peterborough Cathedral. Katherine of Aragon Henry VIII's first wife is buried inside. Mary Queen of Scots was also buried here before being moved to Westminster!

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Where the river runs and taxes were paid
stops.Hint_1: look for the stone house where boats were delayed.
stops.Hint_2: Head down to the River Nene.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Find the small stone building right by the old town bridge. Built in the early 1700s this is the Old Customs House. This was where tolls were collected from the barges bringing goods up the River Nene from the Wash.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: A ringing sound in a village swallowed by the city. Find the pub where the highwayman drank.
stops.Hint_1: Head north to the old village of Werrington.
stops.Hint_2: Look for the traditional thatched pub.
stops.Unlock_Fact: We made it! The Blue Bell in Werrington is one of the oldest pubs in the area. Local legend claims it was a favourite haunt of highwaymen operating on the old Great North Road!

short_description: Decode the cathedral city through kings, queens and river trade.

before_you_go.steps: No required steps are known, though temporary diversions may vary.

before_you_go.footwear: Comfortable walking shoes should be suitable.
before_you_go.dogs: Outdoor route; keep dogs under control and check the final venue’s current dog policy.
before_you_go.pushchairs: Generally possible on public paths; check temporary diversions and busy crossings.
